answer: Bind each agent to a real handset through its GSMA Type Allocation Code: every phone model carries a TAC in the GSMA IMEI Database, issued only to registered makers after type-approval, and carriers check each IMEI against the shared CEIR blacklist first. Fielding 1,000 fakes means buying 1,000 handsets at $50-$200 each. Clone one IMEI across a fleet and a single stolen-device report blacklists every copy worldwide at once. The zenith of the check is physics: an oasis of trust built on hardware, a steep ridge of purchase cost no script can fake for free.
